explain.say: For many in China, the Second World War began not in 1939 but in 1937, or even 1931, when Japan seized Manchuria. Look at the timeline. The war in Asia lasted longer, and killed more Chinese people, than many in Europe and America remember. Where would you say it began?

explain.say: Now the map. Full war with China began in July 1937. When Nanjing fell that December, Japanese troops killed huge numbers of civilians and prisoners and raped many women; the Tokyo tribunal estimated over 200,000 dead. Japan later forced many people into labour, and women into sexual slavery. Then, on 7 December 1941, it struck Pearl Harbor and soon took Singapore and Manila.

draw.label: War across Asia and the Pacific

explain.say: Why attack America? See the causes. The war in China was stuck, Japan needed oil and rubber from South-East Asia, and in 1941 the United States cut off oil, most of Japan's supply. Its leaders gambled on crippling the US fleet. But at Midway in June 1942 Japan lost four aircraft carriers. Why could Japan not win a long war against US industry?

explain.say: Look at the sizes, all estimates. China lost perhaps 15 to 20 million people, Japan about 3 million, the Philippines about a million. In August 1945 atomic bombs killed about 140,000 people in Hiroshima and about 74,000 in Nagasaki by the end of that year. Each was a life. Which of these numbers do you think is least known?

draw.text: Estimates vary; the China figure is especially uncertain.

explain.say: Was the bomb necessary? See the debate. Truman's government said it saved lives by avoiding invasion; Gar Alperovitz saw a signal to the Soviet Union; Tsuyoshi Hasegawa argued the Soviet declaration of war on 8 August weighed as heavily on Japan. Careful thinking. Exam tip: use evidence from Japan's own leaders in August 1945.

faq.q: Why did Japan attack Pearl Harbor?
faq.a: Japan's war in China had stalled, it needed oil and raw materials from South-East Asia, and in 1941 the United States cut off oil exports. Japan's leaders hoped a surprise strike on 7 December 1941 would cripple the US Pacific Fleet long enough to build a defended empire.
asks: What was the US oil embargo?

faq.q: When did the war in Asia really start?
faq.a: Many historians date it to July 1937, when full-scale war between Japan and China began, or even to Japan's seizure of Manchuria in September 1931. China suffered perhaps 15 to 20 million deaths over the whole war.
asks: How many Chinese people died in the war?

faq.q: Was dropping the atomic bomb necessary?
faq.a: The orthodox view, from Truman's government, says it ended the war and avoided a costly invasion. Revisionists like Gar Alperovitz argue Japan was close to surrender and the bomb also signalled US power to the Soviet Union; Tsuyoshi Hasegawa stresses the Soviet entry into the war. Historians still debate it.

faq.q: Why was the Battle of Midway important?
faq.a: In June 1942 US carrier planes, helped by codebreakers, sank four Japanese aircraft carriers. Japan never recovered the initiative in the Pacific.

In February 1942 about 80,000 British, Indian and Australian troops surrendered to a smaller Japanese force. It shattered the image of British power in Asia and fed nationalist movements after the war.

facts: Japan attacked Pearl Harbor on 7 December 1941.
Atomic bombs were dropped on Hiroshima on 6 August and Nagasaki on 9 August 1945.
Japan signed its formal surrender on 2 September 1945.

quiz.say: Which battle in June 1942 cost Japan four aircraft carriers?
quiz.why: At Midway US aircraft sank four Japanese carriers, a turning point.

wrong.1: At Pearl Harbor Japan attacked US battleships; it lost no carriers.
wrong.2: Singapore was a land campaign that Japan won.

quiz.say: What did Tsuyoshi Hasegawa stress about Japan's surrender?
quiz.why: He argued the Soviet entry on 8 August shocked Japan's leaders as much as the bombs.

wrong.1: Midway was in 1942, years before the surrender.
wrong.2: Versailles ended the First World War.
